root_idea.summary: The root centers on طِين, clay formed from earth mixed with water, and related uses of coating, sealing, and material constitution.
root_idea.development: The lexical development extends from clay as a material to coating or sealing with clay, and figuratively to imprinting or forming a person's natural disposition. Related derivatives describe clayiness, clay-working, and objects or persons covered with clay.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The supplied Quranic group is a distinct nominal form and is normalized to the citation form طِين.

senses.definition: Clay: earth mixed with water, including clay or mud after much of its water has departed.
senses.usage_conditions: A concrete noun for the clay material; the supplied Quranic occurrences include creation and forming contexts and vary in case and definiteness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To plaster, coat, or cover something with clay or mud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use; examples include coating roofs, houses or chambers, and walls.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seal a writing or document with clay.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive construction in which the writing is the object sealed with clay.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To create or form someone with an innate disposition toward good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction concerning a person's natural or inborn disposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a person, to make his work or deed good; to perform or execute it well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a person in relation to his work or deed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become defiled or besmeared with clay, earth, or mud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reflexive or intransitive Form V use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Muddy; containing much clay or mud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of a day, place, or land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece or portion of clay used to seal a writing or document.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A more particular use of the noun for the portion of clay applied in sealing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A craving for clay, identified as a kind of malacia.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the expression شَهْوَةُ الطِّينِ, referring to an abnormal appetite for clay.
An idiomatic designation rather than a separate physical-material sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The material substance regarded as what a formed thing consists of.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An abstract material use of طِينَة for the substance underlying a formed object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A natural or native constitution or disposition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use for innate character or temperament.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of or relating to clay; clayey or earthy.
Of or relating to natural or native constitution; natural or native.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival relation to طِينَة in the sense of disposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The art or craft of working with clay, especially plastering with clay or mud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A craft noun derived from the clay-working verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A worker in clay, especially a plasterer who works with clay or mud.
Plastered or coated with clay or mud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a roof or flat house-top and similar clay-coated structures.
